title: Residual history and monitor points: has the run converged?
summary: Normalised residuals against iteration on a log axis, with a tolerance line, above a monitor signal from the flow. Falling residuals are necessary; a flat monitor is the evidence that the answer has stopped changing.

media.alt: Two stacked panels sharing an iteration axis: three falling residual curves on a log scale with a tolerance line, and a monitored outlet temperature settling to a constant value.
media.caption: Reference render with synthetic demonstration data (design-system gallery).

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: Has the run converged?
read_the_figure.axes: Top: x iteration count, y scaled residual (log, 1e-5 to 1) for continuity, momentum and energy; amber dotted line at tolerance 1e-5. Bottom: the monitored outlet temperature T_out in K against the same iteration axis.
look_at: Do all residuals fall below the tolerance line? Which ones, and at which iteration?
Does the monitored quantity settle to a flat line, and when?
Is the 'converged' mark where the residuals actually cross the tolerance?
Is the residual normalised, and by what?
read_the_figure.proves: Residuals that fall by several orders to below tolerance and a monitor that is flat show an iterative solution that has settled. They do not show the solution is accurate: that is discretisation error (F10.8) and modelling error.
if_wrong: Residuals that stall above the tolerance: the iteration will not converge, or the problem is unsteady.
A monitor that still drifts while residuals are small: the residual hides a slow mode.
A 'converged' mark placed before the tolerance crossing, as in this render.

terms.meaning: Imbalance left in a discretised equation when the current iterate is inserted; zero at convergence.
Residual divided by a reference value (first iteration, or a sum of terms), so that it is dimensionless and comparable between equations.
One sweep of the solver; steady problems are solved by iterating until the residual is small.
A quantity of engineering interest, such as an outlet temperature or a force, recorded each iteration.
The residual level below which iteration is stopped.

remember: Residual falls linearly on a semi-log plot for a constant convergence rate.
Always add a monitor: residual and monitor tell different things.
Tolerance is a choice (1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-6): state it.
Converged means residuals under tolerance and monitors flat.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: Position encodes iteration (shared x axis for both panels). In the top panel line style and colour identify the equations, y is logarithmic, an amber dotted line marks the tolerance and a grey dotted vertical line carries the word converged. The bottom panel is a linear trace of one physical quantity with an amber reference value.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: An iterative solver is a sequence of approximations. The residual measures how well the current one satisfies the equations, and a log axis shows how many orders it has fallen. A residual falling slowly is hard to distinguish from stalling without the monitor, and a monitor flat for the wrong reason (a symmetric error) needs the residual. Two panels with a shared iteration axis let the eye connect them.

understand.title: Read this reference render
understand.text: Q1: Which residual is lowest and where does it cross the tolerance? Energy (dash-dot rose) crosses 1e-5 near iteration 1370; momentum ends near 1.3e-5 and continuity at about 3e-5 at iteration 1500, both still above the line. Q2: When does the monitor settle? The outlet temperature overshoots to 419 K at about 120 iterations, then oscillates with decaying amplitude and is flat at 412 K from roughly 900 to 1000 iterations. Q3: Is the converged label correct? No: at iteration 1020 the residuals are about 1e-3 (continuity) to 1e-4 (energy), orders above the tolerance, so by the stated criterion the run is not converged then, although the monitor already is.

understand.title: The must-check list, explained
understand.text: Log y and tolerance line: a log axis shows the orders of magnitude fallen, and the tolerance line is the threshold that makes the word converged a testable statement. Without both the plot has no criterion.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: A residual is relative to its starting value, so a poor initial guess makes it look better than it is. Scaling choices vary between solvers, so tolerances are not portable. A log axis compresses the last orders of magnitude; the monitor line's y range can be chosen to look flat. In this render the 'converged' mark is at 1020 iterations where the residuals are still 1e-3 to 1e-4, and continuity is still above the 1e-5 tolerance at 1500: the annotation is premature.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: Plot the monitor change per iteration on a log axis (a convergence of the answer itself). Use a restart-based check: continue 500 more iterations and see if the monitor moves. Compare the integral balances (mass, energy) as an independent check.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Add a second panel with the net mass imbalance in kg/s and mark the iteration when all three criteria are satisfied.

worked.title: Iterations needed to reach the tolerance
worked.problem: Continuity residual starts at 1 and falls at 0.003 decades per iteration. Estimate the iteration at which it reaches 1e-5, and the same for the energy residual that starts at 0.17 (a deficit of 0.9 decades).

solution.text: Continuity: five decades at 0.003 per iteration.
The energy curve starts about 0.9 decades lower (near 0.13 at iteration 0), so it has less far to fall.

worked.answer: About 1670 iterations for continuity and 1370 for energy: matches the figure, where energy crosses near 1370 and continuity is still above the tolerance at 1500.

analyze.q: The monitor is flat at iteration 900 but the residuals are still 1e-3. Which do you trust?
What would you plot to be sure the answer has stopped changing?
analyze.hint: Look at the change in the monitor per iteration.

evaluate.q: Should the tolerance be 1e-3 for one case and 1e-6 for another?

create: Plot |T_out(n) - T_out(n-1)| on a log axis and mark the tolerance on that axis.
Add an imbalance panel (mass and energy) and require all three before stopping.

checks.answer: They fall by orders of magnitude and the log axis shows how many.

checks.q: A residual falls from 1 to 1e-3 in 300 iterations. How many more to reach 1e-5 at the same rate?
The residuals are below 1e-5 but the monitor still drifts by 0.1 K per 100 iterations. What now?
checks.answer: A slow mode with small residual (poor conditioning, large time scale) means the run is not converged for engineering purposes; continue or accelerate and judge by the monitor and integral balances.
